dedupe_keys.name: strategic sensor placement for the identification of disinfection byproducts from chlorinated drinking water case study in the water distribution network of coimbra portugal

description: The study investigates strategic sensor placement in a calibrated drinking-water distribution network in Coimbra, Portugal. Its native abstract describes a real-world network case and comparisons of algorithms intended to maximize possible detection of disinfection byproducts while minimizing their overall impact. The constrained number of sensors and different performance objectives form the decision problem. A related paper by the same authors explicitly names DBPFinder as the simulation software tested on the Coimbra network. The catalogue links that existing model to this documented application, without treating their descriptions as evidence that identical experiments were performed in both publications. This is a computational network case, not proof of an operational sensor rollout. Numeric detection results, network dimensions, calibration inputs and deployment outcomes are not supplied in the inspected abstracts. The document is publicly described under CC BY 4.0; article bodies and model inputs remain unread. The Zenodo portal provides access to the case document, with limited quantitative detail in its metadata.
